sources.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI: GET/POST Routes, Pydantic Models and Uvicorn

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and a GET "/" route returning {"Hello": "World"}. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in the browser.

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server that runs FastAPI apps
The app.get decorator defines a path for HTTP GET
The --reload flag restarts the server when the file changes

hints: Which two packages do you need to pip install?
The uvicorn command takes the form <module>:<app variable>.
Run `uvicorn main:app --reload`, where main is main.py and app is the FastAPI() instance.
common_mistakes: Running `uvicorn main --reload` without the `:app` part
Naming the file something other than main.py and then running main:app
Forgetting the parentheses in FastAPI()

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: Add `items = []` and a `create_item(item: str)` function decorated with `@app.post("/items")` that appends the item and returns the list. From a second terminal, curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'.

targets.caption: POST handler that appends to items

explanations.topic: Routes define the URLs an app responds to
A plain function argument becomes a query parameter

hints: Which decorator handles HTTP POST requests?
Create a module-level `items = []` and append to it inside the handler.
Pass the value in the URL: `.../items?item=apple`.
common_mistakes: Using @app.get instead of @app.post for the create endpoint
Defining items inside the function so it resets on every request
Forgetting the -X POST flag in curl

steps.title: Get a single item by ID
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with `get_item(item_id: int)` returning `items[item_id]`. Re-add apple and orange after the reload, then curl /items/0 and /items/1.

explanations.topic: Path variables in curly braces map to function arguments
A reload resets the in-memory items list
Type hints make FastAPI convert the parameter type

hints: How do you mark part of the URL as a variable?
Wrap the name in curly braces in the path and use the same name as the function argument.
`@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` and `def get_item(item_id: int)`.
common_mistakes: Testing before re-adding items after the auto-reload emptied the list
Mismatching the path variable name and the function argument name
Leaving out the int type hint, which makes indexing fail on a string

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: Import HTTPException and, in get_item, return the item only if `item_id < len(items)`, otherwise raise `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...)`. Curl a missing index such as /items/3 to see the JSON error.

explanations.topic: A missing item leads to an unhelpful 500 Internal Server Error
HTTP status codes: 4xx is a client error, 404 means Not Found
The detail parameter explains the error

hints: Which HTTP status code means the resource doesn't exist?
Import HTTPException from fastapi and check the index against len(items).
`raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")`
common_mistakes: Using `return HTTPException(...)` instead of `raise`
Forgetting to import HTTPException
Using `<=` in the bounds check, which still causes an IndexError

steps.title: List items with limit parameter
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items")` with `list_items(limit: int = 10)` returning `items[0:limit]`. Add several items, then curl `/items?limit=3` and `/items`.

targets.caption: GET handler with a default limit

explanations.topic: Query parameters are converted to int via the type hint
The same path with a different HTTP method hits a different handler
The default value is defined in the function header

hints: How can a function argument have a default value used when the query param is missing?
Give the argument a type and a default: `limit: int = 10`.
Return a slice: `return items[0:limit]`.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to quote the URL in the shell, so `?` is interpreted by the shell
Omitting the default so `limit` becomes required

steps.title: Define Pydantic Item model
steps.instructions: Import BaseModel from pydantic, create `class Item(BaseModel)` with `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, and use Item in create_item and get_item. POST a JSON body with curl `-d '{"text":"apple"}'`.

explanations.topic: Pydantic models structure and validate data
Model arguments are read from the JSON body, not the query string
Removing a default makes a field required and validated

hints: What class from pydantic do you extend to make a model?
Give Item a `text: str` field and an `is_done: bool = False` field, then use `item: Item` in create_item.
Send JSON with `-d '{"text":"apple"}'` and drop `?item=` from the URL.
common_mistakes: Still sending the item as a query parameter after switching to a model
Missing the `Content-Type: application/json` header
Using single quotes inside the JSON body

steps.title: Add response models
steps.instructions: Add `response_model=Item` to the get_item decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list_items decorator. Confirm uvicorn reloads without errors.

explanations.topic: Response models give front ends a reliable response structure

hints: Where would you tell FastAPI what shape the response has?
It's an argument of the route decorator.
`@app.get("/items/{item_id}", response_model=Item)` and `response_model=list[Item]` for the list.
common_mistakes: Putting response_model in the function signature instead of the decorator
Using `list[Item]` on Python < 3.9 (use `List[Item]` from typing)

steps.title: Test via interactive docs
steps.instructions: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, expand POST /items, click Try it out and execute a request body. Check the response, then try /redoc.

explanations.topic: The free interactive Swagger UI documentation at /docs
/redoc alternative docs and openapi.json schema

hints: FastAPI generates documentation automatically. Which path might it be served on?
Add /docs to the server URL.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, click POST /items, then "Try it out" and "Execute".
common_mistakes: Visiting /doc instead of /docs
Stopping the uvicorn server before opening the docs
